name: DOOM Music Extension
author: Thomas Reetz

provenance.from: kyzer.me.uk/amos/amosfactory/dme.lha, retrieved 2026-08-12 and held in the corpus at sources/kyzer-dme/. 692,668 bytes, sha256 e9f0baa035f6c38606bb6d6ccad4924d1e33b03e206a6c6ca31dc949c3312338 -- the "676Kb - LhA" the AMOS extension list promised. That list's own download link was lha/dme.lha on amigau.com and the Wayback Machine never captured it; kyzer's AMOS Factory mirror had it.
provenance.note: SLOT 15, AND THE BINARY SAYS SO: routine 0 stores its AllocMem'd block with `move.l d0,$1d8(a5)` and returns `moveq #$e,d0`, and ($1d8-$f8)/16+1 is 15 on the ExtAdr layout (+Equ.s:1157) with $e the slot zero-based. Jens Vang Petersen's AMOS extension pages, 1997-1998, said 15 too, and also record "PRO Version: 2.00", no TC version, and Public Domain. IT REFUSES TO LOAD ANYWHERE ELSE: the first instruction after the register save is `cmp.l #$41506578,d1` --- the ASCII `APex` --- and a mismatch returns -1 without allocating anything.
provenance.redistribution: Public Domain per the extension list. Not redistributed by amos-ts; fixtures/ is gitignored.

findings: The real binary replaced an AMOSTools stub and proved all 233 token rows, 184 distinct names, slot 15, and the 37 unreachable nop padding rows. DME contains three players (ProTracker, THX and Player 6.1A) plus raw-sample playback; it opens twelve external players: eleven DME_* libraries and playsid.library. All fifteen music formats and the sampler are implemented. Each held DME library is audited through its complete resident vector table and its format, replay and mixer modules; the extension veneer is covered in src/runtime/dme.test.ts. Shared THX and P61 spellings remain slot-qualified because their ids differ from the standalone extensions. OctaMix has no surviving compatible module in the corpus, so its arithmetic is binary-backed but cannot receive a real-module listening oracle.
notes: Plays fifteen tracker and chip-music formats plus raw samples, one keyword block per player.
